subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Health-Related Fitness and Personal Activity Planning
essentialQuestion: How do I build an activity plan that fits my body and my life?

prompts.prompt: Name the movement cues for components of health-related fitness and explain what each one does.
Show, describe, or diagram judging effort without measurement. A demonstration, a spoken description, and a drawing are equally valid.
Apply building cardiorespiratory endurance enjoyably in a new movement task at a challenge level you select. Control and cue use are assessed, not speed, distance, or count.
A made-up learner is struggling with muscular strength, endurance, and flexibility. Identify the likely cue or decision at fault, correct it, and explain why the correction helps.
Connect components of health-related fitness with planning activity I will actually keep doing. Explain how one supports the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a two-week personal activity plan based on enjoyment, access, safety, and recovery. No weight, body measurement, calorie, timing, or fitness-test target may appear in it.
Describe one way you adapted a task so it worked for you, and one activity from this unit you would choose to do again. There is no wrong answer here.

adaptationChoices: Access supports may change equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. Using the adapted alternative is a full-credit path, never a reduced one.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. Using the adapted alternative is a full-credit path, never a reduced one.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
